text:
Kasperi Kapanen has quietly become useful in Edmonton. He's playing 18 minutes a night, more than ever, and seven of his 10 points have come on the power play. That's a big share for a winger who isn't usually a first-unit guy, and it's a sign of how much the Oilers have needed bodies while Zach Hyman was out.

He's been physical too, 42 hits in 19 games, and he fought in the loss to Anaheim on a night he also scored on the power play. The five-on-five picture is flatter: Edmonton has about 49% of the expected goals with him out there, and Evolving-Hockey had his on-ice offense in the bottom 5% of forwards last season.

The skating is the standout tool. His top speed this season is the fastest in our tracking, a 100th percentile mark, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him exiting his zone with the puck 80% of the time. At 17.9% shooting, his goal total is running a bit warm. Our range: about 21 goals and 46 points if the role sticks, and the role is the thing to watch now that Hyman is back.
headline: Kasperi Kapanen has found a power-play home
